featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Gala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience.

The person running this photo studio is extremely rude and unprofessional. I went there specifically to get U.S. visa photos, and he confidently claimed that he knows exactly how the U.S. visa photo requirements work.

However, the photos he took were clearly pixelated and of very poor quality, and they were rejected at the embassy. Because of this mistake, we had to take new photos at the embassy itself and pay an additional premium fee, which could have easily been avoided if the photos were taken properly in the first place.

When we went back and informed him about the rejection and the poor photo quality, instead of taking responsibility he simply said “that’s the embassy’s problem, they reject photos all the time” and refused to acknowledge the issue. If he already knows that photos taken at his studio are getting rejected frequently, then he should inform customers beforehand instead of confidently claiming expertise.

The amount we paid may only be ₹200, but the point is not the money — it’s about basic professionalism and customer respect. Customers should not have to waste their time and money because of poor service and misinformation.

On top of that, his attitude towards customers is extremely rude and dismissive. No willingness to listen, no accountability, and no respect.

I would strongly advise people to avoid this studio for visa photos or any important documentation photos.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Yelligetti
featured_reviews.review_text:
We enquired about a 5th birthday of kids photography package. Before confirming, we simply requested to visit the studio and check the clothes included in the package. But instead they asked us to pay the advance first and also bring backup clothes in case theirs don’t work.
How can anyone pay for a service without even seeing what they are paying for? This approach felt very unprofessional and not customer-friendly.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi,

Thank you for taking out time to write this. This allows us the opportunity to also make you understand on a public forum that having a process as a business doesn't make us unprofessional. Unfortunately, today people look down upon photographers and the photography business on the whole, like we deserve to have no rules and we cannot be respected. We are a private service where we take on clients only upon booking. We are not a walk-in retail store, nor are we a clothing store. We are a photography business and our primary job is to click beautiful photos.

Coming to paying for something you were not shown. Right from sharing our studio video, to sharing links to our past work as well as showing you photos of the outfits we have, we did everything that could give you a very clear idea of what you're paying for. So please refrain from making false claims.

If we are offering clothing options, it is just a move we made to make life easy for clients and to ensure your photos look good. However, it is not unfair of us to ask you to carry your options and we to do also to make sure that at the final hour you are not left with 0 options. We buy clothes from the same stores as any parent does for their kids. And as long as the child wears clothes of their age and they don't need to downsize or wear bigger sizes, our outfits fit. But saying that us asking you to carry clothes as a back up is unprofessional is strange and impractical of you. 

We have rules like booking in place so that nobody walks in on someone's shoot and no client has to wait around our premises for their chance. If taking advance booking so that you and your family doesn't have to face any discomfort is unprofessional and not customer friendly, then please tell us if taking people in randomly, cancelling a shoot because another client is paying more and indulging in such unethical behaviour is professional? 

It's great you have a medium here to voice your unhappiness. But at least care to be honest, rational and practical before coming down a public forum. We are also customers to other businesses and we would rather appreciate someone who works with a system process than run them down. It is sad to see an educated lot disregard systems & processes.
